title: GovEagle adds Unified Assets to the opportunity workspace
summary: GovEagle's new Assets tab holds every document for an opportunity, from the RFP to your pricing sheets, grouped into upload and SharePoint sources.
body_markdown:
Every document for an opportunity now lives in one Assets tab, from the government's RFP to your own pricing spreadsheets. Unified Assets is in beta.


## What changed


Solicitation documents, reference documents and your team's working files used to sit in separate parts of an opportunity. Now:


- **One tab for the whole bid.** The RFP, SOW, PWS, amendments and Q&A sit beside your technical approaches, past performance volumes, pricing spreadsheets and compliance matrices.
- **Organized by source.** Upload sources hold files you add to GovEagle. SharePoint sources stay in sync with a folder your team already works in.
- **Nothing lost.** Existing solicitation files, reference documents and files imported from SAM.gov or Salesforce appear as their own sources.
- **Chat starts with the bid's files.** When you chat inside an opportunity, GovEagle checks its Assets first and uses the Content Library for supporting material such as past performance.


## Who it helps


Proposal managers who are tired of asking which folder holds the current version, and admins who want every bid set up the same way.


## How Unified Assets works


1. Admins choose the sources every new opportunity starts with in **Settings → Opportunity Management → Assets** , up to 20.
2. When someone creates an opportunity, those sources are already on the form. Upload files or paste a SharePoint folder link.
3. In the **Assets** tab, add files, link more folders or create a document from a template.


Get GovCon capture and proposal insights in your inbox.


## Where it fits


Assets is part of[GovEagle's capture workspace](https://www.goveagle.com/solutions/bd-capture) . For how folder access carries over from SharePoint, read[access control and SharePoint permissions for proposal teams](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/access-control-govcon-proposals) .


## What it doesn't do


- **It doesn't replace the Content Library.** Assets belong to one opportunity and don't affect others.
- **SharePoint write access depends on your setup.** With read-only permission, the source is a mirror you can view and chat with.
- **Default sources apply to new opportunities only.** Existing ones keep theirs.


## Get started


Unified Assets is in beta. To turn it on for your organization, emailsupport@goveagle.com .
